stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist was hospitalised for much of the renewal cycle and completed only part of her required continuing education. She wants to renew. What does the regulation direct her to do?

choices.text: Self-certify the shortfall on the renewal application and renew without further steps.
Renew now and complete the missing contact hours within the following calendar year.
Submit a sworn detailed statement of the extenuating circumstances for the Board to determine.
Apply for retired status until the missing contact hours can be completed.
Request that her employer certify the extenuating circumstances directly to the Board.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 4.03(6) provides that a registrant who has failed to complete the requisite contact hours shall submit to the Board a detailed statement, signed under the penalties of perjury, setting out the extenuating circumstances with detail and specificity, and the Board then determines whether renewal is granted and notifies the applicant of its determination and reasons.

choice_analysis.A: Self-certification of a shortfall is not the mechanism provided.
choice_analysis.B: There is no make-up allowance in the following year; hours may not be carried over.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: a sworn detailed statement, with the Board determining the outcome.
choice_analysis.D: Retired status bars practice and is not a continuing education mechanism.
choice_analysis.E: The statement is the registrant's own and is signed under the penalties of perjury.

related_facts: A registrant is not required to complete continuing education in the calendar year of graduation from an approved school.
explanation.mpje_trap: Extenuating circumstances are a Board determination on a sworn statement, not a self-applied exemption.

reasoning_steps: Identify the shortfall as a continuing education failure rather than a lapse in registration
Submit a sworn detailed statement and leave the determination to the Board
